generalization_statements.description: Generalization statements at three levels of ambition.

statement.description: The generalization statement. What population/context does the theory (or part of it) apply to?

confidence.description: How confident is this generalization based on the data?

confidence_rationale.description: Why this confidence level (e.g., 'documented across 7 of 9 cases with variation in context').

limitations.description: What limits this generalization? What would need to be true for it to NOT hold?

boundary_conditions.description: Conditions that define where the theory applies and where it does not.

condition.description: The boundary condition. E.g., 'Participants must be mid-career professionals facing technological displacement.'

effect_on_theory.description: How the theory changes if this condition is not met. 'Theory does not apply', 'Core process changes from X to Y', 'Property Z loses relevance', etc.

derived_from_category.description: Which category or property reveals this boundary condition.

conceptual_transferability.description: How transferable are the CONCEPTS (categories, properties) to other populations? Independent of whether the full theory transfers.

populational_transferability.description: How transferable are the full FINDINGS to other populations?

overall_assessment.description: Narrative synthesis: to whom does this theory apply? What are the key boundaries? 3-5 sentences.

context_bound_categories.description: Categories that are too tied to the specific study context to generalize.

specificity_rationale.description: Why this category does not generalize beyond the studied context.

suggested_future_research.description: Populations or contexts where the theory should be tested/elaborated next.
